\section[la admiración]{la admiración — admiration}

\label{lesson:ES-C720-admiracion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for worry, then the Spanish for worried.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la admiración}
\textbf{la admiración} — \textquotedblleft{}admiration\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Siento admiración por los médicos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I feel admiration for doctors.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Signo de admiración} — exclamation mark.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{admiración} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{admīrātiō} (EtymDB), built on \emph{admīrārī} \textquotedblleft{}to wonder at\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{mīrārī} \textquotedblleft{}to marvel\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la admiración}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la admiración}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la admiración}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for worry, then the Spanish for worried, then say \emph{la admiración} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la admiración mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Admiration\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[admirar]{admirar — to admire}

\label{lesson:ES-C720-admirar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for worried, then the Spanish for admiration.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: admirar}
\textbf{admirar} — \textquotedblleft{}to admire\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Admiro mucho a mi profesora.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I really admire my teacher.}
\end{quote}

Takes personal \emph{a} with people: \emph{admiro a mi madre}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{admirar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{admīrārī} \textquotedblleft{}to wonder at\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); \emph{mirar} \textquotedblleft{}to look\textquotedblright{} is the inherited form of \emph{mīrārī}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{admirar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{admirar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{admirar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for worried, then the Spanish for admiration, then say \emph{admirar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does admirar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To admire\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[agradecido]{agradecido — grateful}

\label{lesson:ES-C720-agradecido}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for admiration, then the Spanish for to admire.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: agradecido}
\textbf{agradecido} — \textquotedblleft{}grateful\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Te estoy muy agradecido.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I am very grateful to you.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Estar agradecido por algo}. \emph{Muy agradecido} — much obliged.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{agradecido} is the participle of \emph{agradecer}, built on old \emph{gradecer}, from \emph{grado} \textquotedblleft{}goodwill\textquotedblright{}, which is usually traced to Latin \emph{grātum} \textquotedblleft{}pleasing\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agradecido}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agradecido}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{agradecido}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for admiration, then the Spanish for to admire, then say \emph{agradecido} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does agradecido mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Grateful\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[la gratitud]{la gratitud — gratitude}

\label{lesson:ES-C720-gratitud}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to admire, then the Spanish for grateful.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la gratitud}
\textbf{la gratitud} — \textquotedblleft{}gratitude\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Quiero expresar mi gratitud a todos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I want to express my gratitude to everyone.}
\end{quote}

More formal than \emph{el agradecimiento}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gratitud} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{grātitūdō} (EtymDB), built on \emph{grātus} \textquotedblleft{}thankful, pleasing\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la gratitud}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la gratitud}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la gratitud}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to admire, then the Spanish for grateful, then say \emph{la gratitud} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[apreciar]{apreciar — to appreciate, to value}

\label{lesson:ES-C720-apreciar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for grateful, then the Spanish for gratitude.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: apreciar}
\textbf{apreciar} — \textquotedblleft{}to appreciate, to value\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Aprecio mucho tu ayuda.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I really appreciate your help.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Aprecio a mis compañeros} — I am fond of my colleagues.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{apreciar} is a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{appretiāre} \textquotedblleft{}to put a price on\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{pretium} \textquotedblleft{}price\textquotedblright{}, the source of \emph{precio}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for grateful, then the Spanish for gratitude, then say \emph{apreciar} again
\end{itemize}
